newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan energy minister to visit Iraq next month.
newsitem.headline: Jordan energy minister to visit Iraq next month.

text.p: Jordan's Energy Minister Mohammed al-Hourani will visit Baghdad next month to discuss oil pipeline and exploration projects and review progress of an oil deal which supplies Jordan with its energy needs, officials said.
They said Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed, stopping off in Amman on Sunday on the way to Europe, discussed Hourani's coming visit to Baghdad.

"We discussed the preparations for the visit (of the Jordanian minister) to Baghdad in the first half of next month," Rasheed told reporters before leaving for Madrid to discuss energy cooperation with Spanish officials.
He is later due in Vienna to participate at a conference of OPEC oil ministers between June 25-27.

Rasheed said he and Hourani would "discuss practical steps in the fields of cooperation between us and any paragraphs that relate to the Iraqi-Jordanian accord relating to supply of Jordan with crude and products."

"We will also evaluate projects of joint cooperation by intensifying our efforts and opening new avenues of bilateral cooperation," Rasheed said referring to joint ventures such as a proposed oil pipeline and a joint exploration firm.
These projects, which have been discussed intermittently over the years, are on hold until the lifting of U.N. economic sanctions imposed on Iraq after its invasion of Kuwait.
Iraq supplies Jordan with 75,000 bpd of crude and products in return for Jordanian industrial exports under an annual trade protocol which is exempt from the U.N. sanctions.
Jordan's industrialist lobby is pushing their government to seek U.N. sanction exemptions on imports of Iraq's competitively priced urea and sulphur.
